13 years ago, Ivan Zhao (@ivanhzhao) started Notion so anyone could make software without knowing how to code. Now AI agents do that out of the box. Rebuilding Notion for that world is one of the hardest things he’s ever done. Ivan and I talked at Thesis: 2027, @Every’s conference on what great human work looks like after automation. I came away thinking Notion is a dark-horse candidate as one of the most important companies at the app layer in AI. Here’s what we talked about: • How Notion went from pre-AI to AI-native. In late 2022, Ivan and his cofounder locked themselves in a hotel room and shipped their first AI product weeks before ChatGPT—even while people inside the company thought AI was a fad like crypto. After two years grinding on agents, they realized everyone is building agents now, so Notion’s unique edge had to come back to its core. • Why context outlasts UI and workflows. For the past 15 years, software meant a company picking one workflow and building buttons around it—something an agent can now vibe code on demand. Ivan says Notion isn’t married to the UI anymore. What lasts is a team’s data, semantics, and context, and Notion wants to be the keeper of that context for both humans and the next billion knowledge workers, most of whom he expects will be agents. • Legos versus clay for vibe coding. Coding agents hand you clay—granular code that falls apart when you try to build a tall tower without expertise. Notion is leaning into the Legos: opening its UI pattern libraries to agents while taking care of permissions, syncing, and collaboration under the hood, alongside Ivan’s framework for what you should vibe code yourself versus leave to crafted software. • The TikTokification of AI—and keeping human understanding. Ivan admits he catches himself chatting with Claude instead of reading on his Kindle, getting grossed out after 10 minutes like he’s on TikTok. His deeper warning for builders is not to surrender understanding when agents write code inside black boxes—which is why Notion’s own teams went back to Kanban boards to visualize and orchestrate their agents’ work. This is a must-listen for anyone transitioning their company to the AI age.
